---
title: "Day 1 – Open research and the case"
---
::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" icon=false}
**Slides.** The deck of the three days is in preparation, and the [slides page](slides.qmd) shows the deck of the earlier three-day course meanwhile.
:::

Day 1 builds the ground on which the other two days stand: why the reproduction, the robustness and the replication of published results became questions for the field, where the data and the code of studies are kept and found, what SCORE and Multi100 set out to do and how they did it, and the paper of the original author (OA) read in full, with the methods on which its claim rests. The last session installs the tools and downloads the data that days 2 and 3 need. The day runs as four sessions of ninety minutes.

## 1. Credibility and the three Rs

[Open the resources page](../../resources.qmd){.btn .btn-primary target="_blank"}

The first session asks what a claim is for and why the field speaks of a crisis, and sets out the evidence on reproducibility, robustness and replicability. The resources page holds the core readings and the [glossary](../../resources.qmd#glossary) of the terms of the session.

## 2. Repositories and data sources

[Read Reproducibility repositories](../../companion/repositories.qmd){.btn .btn-primary target="_blank"} [Read Social science data sources](../../companion/data-sources.qmd){.btn .btn-outline-primary target="_blank"} [Read SCORE and Multi100 in the case study](../../cases/eu-frames/index.qmd#sec-score){.btn .btn-outline-primary target="_blank"}

The second session covers where the data and the code of a study are deposited and how they are found, cited and downloaded, from the OSF and Dataverse to the survey archives. It ends on SCORE and Multi100, with their aims and their designs.

## 3. The paper in detail

[Read the original study in the case study](../../cases/eu-frames/index.qmd#sec-study){.btn .btn-primary target="_blank"} [Read the exercise overview](../../cases/eu-frames/exercise.qmd){.btn .btn-outline-primary target="_blank"}

The third session discusses the paper of the OA in full: the question, the data, the measures, the models and the claim as SCORE selected it, with the methodological grounding of each choice.

## 4. Tools and data

[Install R and the workspace](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/setup.html){.btn .btn-primary target="_blank"} [Download the Eurobarometer files](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/setup.html#the-eurobarometer-files-for-the-individual-level-work){.btn .btn-outline-primary target="_blank"}

The last session installs R, Quarto and an IDE and checks them, downloads the workspace of the case and runs its check script, and downloads the Eurobarometer files of the waves that the paper used. The files come from the GESIS archive under a free account and on terms that do not allow the files to be passed on, and [the GESIS archive](../../companion/data-sources.qmd#sec-gesis) in the module on data sources takes the download screen by screen. The [help page](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/help.html) lists the problems that other participants have met, and the [module on the IDE](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/tools/ide.html) on the AR4DS site shows where everything is in the IDE that you chose.

**By the end of the day** you can say what the claim is and how the paper supports it, and where its data and the materials of its reanalyses are kept, and you have a working installation with the workspace and the raw data in place.
